questions.prompt: A line fitted to rewards 0.2, 0.5, 0.8 at actions 0, 1, 2. Estimate at action 4? (one decimal)
Estimates (0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5) at actions 0..3, support {0, 1}. Penalty weight needed so action 1 beats action 3 under Q - lambda*distance? (two decimals)
questions.explanation: Action 3 has distance 2 from action 1: (1.5 - 0.5)/2 = 0.5 (action 2: (1.0-0.5)/1 = 0.5 as well).

questions.prompt: Which of these dataset facts best tells you that a learned action is unsupported?
options: Its estimated value is high compared to other actions
Its estimated value is low compared to other actions
It is chosen by the greedy policy of the learner
Zero or very few logged samples at nearby state-action pairs
questions.explanation: Support is about data coverage, not about the value the model assigns.

questions.prompt: n = 9 samples, sigma = 0.6, c = 2. Penalty c*sigma/sqrt(n)? (two decimals)
A tabular offline learner initialises unseen Q-values to 0 and all real rewards are negative. What is the likely result of taking max over all actions?
options: Nothing happens, since defaults are ignored by the maximum
The learner becomes more conservative about unseen actions
Unseen actions look best because 0 exceeds every real value
The Q-values converge to the true values of the policy
questions.explanation: Real Q-values are negative, so the unseen default 0 is the maximum and attracts the policy.

Setting lambda (or c) very large in a conservative offline method tends to
options: ignore the dataset and follow only the penalty it adds
find the global optimum, even for actions outside the data
make the value function exact at every action in the task
reproduce the best supported choice, like behaviour cloning
questions.explanation: With a huge penalty only supported actions can win.

always larger than the naive greedy regret
